annotation.title_clean: Trust in Robot Benchmarking and Benchmarking for Trustworthy Robots
annotation.title_en: Trust in Robot Benchmarking and Benchmarking for Trustworthy Robots
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Thoduka, S.; Nair, D.; Caleb-Solly, P.; Dragone, M.; Cavallo, F.; Hochgeschwender, N.
annotation.venue: Producing Artificial Intelligent Systems (Studies in Computational Intelligence 1150), Springer
annotation.summary_en: Book chapter proposing a progressive, iterative robot benchmarking process through competitions (dataset-based, remote robot, field evaluations), modelled on the ML lifecycle and illustrated with the HEART-MET competition. It adds non-functional criteria such as fault tolerance, robustness and social acceptance to support trustworthy robots.
key_provisions_or_claims: Proposes staged benchmarking from datasets and simulation to remote and field tests, suited to TRL 4-7.
Benchmarks should evaluate non-functional qualities (fault tolerance, adaptability, robustness, social acceptance) as well as functional ones.
Out-of-distribution data, failure scenarios and user studies should be built into benchmarks.
Builds on RoCKIn functional and task benchmarks and the European Robotics League.
Existing competitions such as RoboCup and ERL focus on functional aspects and ignore moral trust.
